To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the private business case is strong for commercial demand response for providing spinning reserve; and (ii) avoided carbon emission damages from providing spinning reserve using demand response could justify incentives for demand response resources to participate.

1) DR for spinning reserve is a potentially attractive business for DR aggregators, 2) DR for spinning reserves is most profitable for customers with long operating hours, such that end uses like grocery stores and lodging are more profitable than other commercial customers, 3) the business case for DR for spinning reserve varies significantly by customer end use and business segment, and 4) avoided damages from carbon emissions may justify incentives for DR to provide spinning reserve.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economics of demand response (DR) programs for spinning reserve in California.
the economics of commercial demand side resources, and in particular, demand response.
the economic feasibility of demand response (DR) resources for spinning reserve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the economic and environmental benefits of DR for spinning reserve are substantial.
the economics of commercial DR for spinning reserve are favorable for some end uses and business sectors.
demand side resources can play a key role in the grid, but the business case needs to be carefully examined for each application and end use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DR for spinning reserve can be economically attractive, especially for steady end uses and long operating hour business segments.
the economics for demand response resources to provide spinning reserve are promising, and the potential for carbon emission damages to provide incentives is also promising.
demand side resources are a viable alternative to traditional generation resources, especially for spinning reserve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant opportunities for DR to provide spinning reserve.
the economics of demand response are highly dependent on the end use, and that the end use is often not specified when the potential of DR is discussed.
the business case for demand response (DR) is highly variable depending on end use and customer type.
